verses.text: For the divisions of the doorkeepers: of the Korahites, Meshelemiah the son of Kore, of the sons of Asaph.
Meshelemiah had sons: Zechariah the firstborn, Jediael the second, Zebadiah the third, Jathniel the fourth,
Elam the fifth, Jehohanan the sixth, and Eliehoenai the seventh.
Obed-Edom had sons: Shemaiah the firstborn, Jehozabad the second, Joah the third, Sacar the fourth, Nethanel the fifth,
Ammiel the sixth, Issachar the seventh, and Peullethai the eighth; for God blessed him.
Sons were also born to Shemaiah his son, who ruled over the house of their father; for they were mighty men of valor.
The sons of Shemaiah: Othni, Rephael, Obed, and Elzabad, whose brothers were valiant men, Elihu, and Semachiah.
All these were of the sons of Obed-Edom: they and their sons and their brothers, able men in strength for the service; sixty-two of Obed-Edom.
Meshelemiah had sons and brothers, valiant men, eighteen.
Also Hosah, of the children of Merari, had sons: Shimri the chief (for though he was not the firstborn, yet his father made him chief),
Hilkiah the second, Tebaliah the third, and Zechariah the fourth: all the sons and brothers of Hosah were thirteen.
Of these were the divisions of the doorkeepers, even of the chief men, having offices like their brothers, to minister in Yahweh’s house.
They cast lots, the small as well as the great, according to their fathers’ houses, for every gate.
The lot eastward fell to Shelemiah. Then for Zechariah his son, a wise counselor, they cast lots; and his lot came out northward.
To Obed-Edom southward; and to his sons the storehouse.
To Shuppim and Hosah westward, by the gate of Shallecheth, at the causeway that goes up, watchman opposite watchman.
Eastward were six Levites, northward four a day, southward four a day, and for the storehouse two and two.
For Parbar westward, four at the causeway, and two at Parbar.
These were the divisions of the doorkeepers; of the sons of the Korahites, and of the sons of Merari.
Of the Levites, Ahijah was over the treasures of God’s house and over the treasures of the dedicated things.
The sons of Ladan, the sons of the Gershonites belonging to Ladan, the heads of the fathers’ households belonging to Ladan the Gershonite: Jehieli.
The sons of Jehieli: Zetham, and Joel his brother, over the treasures of Yahweh’s house.
Of the Amramites, of the Izharites, of the Hebronites, of the Uzzielites:
and Shebuel the son of Gershom, the son of Moses, was ruler over the treasures.
His brothers: of Eliezer, Rehabiah his son, and Jeshaiah his son, and Joram his son, and Zichri his son, and Shelomoth his son.

This Shelomoth and his brothers were over all the treasures of the dedicated things, which David the king, and the heads of the fathers’ households, the captains over thousands and hundreds, and the captains of the army, had dedicated.
They dedicated some of the plunder won in battles to repair Yahweh’s house.

All that Samuel the seer, and Saul the son of Kish, and Abner the son of Ner, and Joab the son of Zeruiah, had dedicated, whoever had dedicated anything, it was under the hand of Shelomoth, and of his brothers.
Of the Izharites, Chenaniah and his sons were for the outward business over Israel, for officers and judges.

Of the Hebronites, Hashabiah and his brothers, men of valor, one thousand seven hundred, had the oversight of Israel beyond the Jordan westward, for all the business of Yahweh, and for the service of the king.

Of the Hebronites was Jerijah the chief, even of the Hebronites, according to their generations by fathers’ households. They were sought for in the fortieth year of the reign of David, and mighty men of valor were found among them at Jazer of Gilead.

His brothers, men of valor, were two thousand seven hundred, heads of fathers’ households, whom king David made overseers over the Reubenites, the Gadites, and the half-tribe of the Manassites, for every matter pertaining to God, and for the affairs of the king.

footnotes.content: Meshelemiah opens these doorkeeper families—a line whose name means 'God recompenses.' Even in a list of gatekeepers, the Lord is naming those who tend His threshold, honoring them with remembrance. There's gentleness in how God sees the faithful in hidden work.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Zechariah stands first among Meshelemiah's sons—'the Lord remembers.' What tender grace, that the firstborn of a gatekeeper carries a name binding him to God's fidelity. Even the order of a father's children speaks of the Lord's steadiness.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Seven sons listed—the number of completion. Eliehoenai, the seventh, bears a name meaning 'my eyes are toward God.' A gatekeeper's eyes turn rightly: not inward or outward alone, but first toward Him who dwells within.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Obed-Edom's family continues the doorkeeper line. We met this man before—the one David honored for his faithfulness when the Ark rested in his home. Now his sons inherit both blessing and service. Faithfulness flows like water through generations.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: 'For God blessed him'—eight sons, each stronger for the blessing resting on their father's house. The text itself pauses here to mark it: God does not leave His servants childless or weak. Peullethai, the eighth, carries a name few could pronounce, yet he belongs fully to the blessed line.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Shemaiah, Obed-Edom's son, ruled over the household—not by rank alone, but by the strength of godly character. His name means 'God has heard.' A father who listens to the Lord raises sons others will follow.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Othni, Rephael, Obed, Elzabad—four names of substance among Shemaiah's sons, and their brothers equally strong. The Lord builds His house not with exceptional giants, but with faithful people of steady valor, generation after generation.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Sixty-two souls from Obed-Edom's line serve at the gates. A quiet army of fidelity—not warriors conquering kingdoms, but keepers standing firm, day after day, tending the threshold of God's house. That too is valor.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Meshelemiah brings eighteen souls—fewer than Obed-Edom, yet the text names him first. The Lord does not measure faithfulness by numbers alone. A smaller household, wholly devoted, shines as bright as a larger one.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Shimri rises as chief, though not the firstborn—his father chose him by character, not custom. When a man's faithfulness speaks louder than birthright, the Lord's order shows through. Shimri means 'my watchfulness,' and the role fit the name.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Hilkiah, Tebaliah, Zechariah—Hosah's sons, thirteen in all, the number of God's kingdom breaking into fragments. Each name carries weight: 'My portion is God,' 'God is my salvation,' 'The Lord remembers.' Small names, profound anchors.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: These divisions—gatekeeper families—receive their dignity through service. 'Like their brothers, to minister in the Lord's house.' No hierarchy of holiness, only shared work tending what God treasures. A humble posture opens wide the door to His presence.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: They cast lots for the gates—small and great alike drawing by the Lord's hidden hand. Even the assignment of gates shows no favoritism in the sight of God. Every post belongs to Him, and every keeper is equally seen.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The east gate falls to Shelemiah; Zechariah, 'a wise counselor,' goes north. Wisdom and direction intertwine—a counselor posted where dawn breaks, where new light first enters. The placement itself is a teaching.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Obed-Edom guards the south; his sons hold the storehouse. This man, once blessed by the Ark's presence, now guards treasure—sacred gifts and the riches of the temple. Blessing and responsibility walk together.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Shuppim and Hosah stand west, by Shallecheth Gate, watchman opposite watchman. Even pairs of gatekeepers mirror mutual care—each sees the other, neither alone. God's house is tended by those who watch over one another.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Six Levites east, four north, four south—a mathematical beauty, an ordered rhythm guarding the Lord's threshold from every direction. The details matter because a house of prayer deserves a thoughtful, faithful watch.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Parbar westward holds four gatekeepers, with two more at the storehouse approach. Every corner accounted for, every soul belonging somewhere. The Lord misses no one and leaves no gate unwatched.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The divisions are named: Korahites and Merarites—two Levite families, united in service. Different lineages, one calling. That's how the body of Christ works: diverse in origin, whole in purpose.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Ahijah watches over treasures of God's house and dedicated things—a post of rare trust. To hold what others have offered to the Lord is to stand in the holy middle ground between gift and giver, human generosity and divine use.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Jehieli heads the Gershonite treasurers—his name means 'God will carry off my iniquity.' A man bearing a name of mercy oversees what the Lord deems precious. There's poetry in the pairing.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Zetham and Joel, brothers, stand as joint stewards over the Lord's treasures. Even wealth and precious things are safer in hands that share the burden—and the joy—of guardianship together.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Four families of Levites arise now: Amramites, Izharites, Hebronites, Uzzielites—a genealogical roll honoring the deep roots of priesthood. Every family matters to the Lord's reckoning; none slips into shadow.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Shebuel, grandson of Moses, rules the treasures—Moses, who led the exodus, whose line carries forward in temple service. Even the greatest prophets' descendants find their calling in humble faithfulness, not in repeating their ancestor's fame.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Eliezer's line branches through generations—Rehabiah, Jeshaiah, Joram, Zichri, Shelomoth. Each name is a link in a chain of trust, descendants of Moses standing as stewards of the temple's wealth. Faithfulness multiplies through the generations.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Shelomoth and his brothers guard what David, his generals, and the people dedicated—war spoils turned to sacred use. A king's pride and a people's worship flow through these treasurers' hands. They hold not just gold, but the hopes of a nation seeking God.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Battle-won plunder becomes repair and rebuilding of the Lord's house—swords beaten into tools, conquest turned to service. The Lord takes even human striving and reshapes it toward His restoration.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Samuel, Saul, Abner, Joab—names of prophets and warriors, all under Shelomoth's care now. What they conquered or judged, he safeguards as memorial. The Lord remembers every offering, every hand that gave, from the least to the greatest.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Chenaniah and his sons 'for the outward business over Israel, for officers and judges'—they bring the temple's order into the civil realm. Sacred and secular service blend when all is done before God's watching eye.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Hashabiah, 'the Lord is my riches,' leads 1,700 Hebronites east of the Jordan—a vast territory overseen by men of valor. The Lord extends His order far beyond the temple walls; His kingdom reaches to every corner.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Jerijah, chief of Hebronites, was sought for 'in the fortieth year of David's reign'—found among the mighty at Jazer in Gilead. Even in a place remote, the Lord raises up those He has prepared. His eye misses no faithful servant.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Readers today hear an echo in this description: 2,700 men of valor tending to 'every matter pertaining to God, and for the affairs of the king.' How often we separate the sacred from the daily—yet here they intertwine, suggesting that faithfulness in all things is faithfulness to Him. As of 2026-10, the Lord still calls us to that wholeness.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight
